diagnosis.root_cause: Progressive attenuation on this customer's fibre path, likely a degraded connector, splice, or drop fibre. RX power declined from the normal range around -19.6 dBm to critical levels below -28 dBm while distance remained constant, TX power and laser bias stayed healthy, and all peers on the PON remained normal. The frequent short sessions and periods of unavailability are symptoms of the degrading optical link.
evidence: Current ONU telemetry shows RX power at -28.31 dBm in the critical range, with a live probe reading of -28.94 dBm.
The seven-day RX trend falls steadily from approximately -19.6 dBm, which is normal, to below -28 dBm, so this is a genuine decline rather than a link that was marginal from the beginning.
Distance remains constant at 310 m throughout the telemetry window, ruling out a path-record or geometry change.
TX power remains near 2.3-2.4 dBm and TX bias current remains stable around 11.5-11.8 mA, ruling out laser degradation.
All tested peer ONUs on EPON0/2 are online with normal optical levels, so the problem is confined to this customer's path rather than the PON, splitter, port, or OLT.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, has normal CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime, and all eight PONs are reported healthy.
The ONU currently responds and is online, but the critical and declining RX level explains intermittent service and the complaint that it is dead for much of the day.

The customer has 14 sessions in 24 hours with short average duration, but the declining optical trend takes precedence; the session churn is a consequence of the fibre degradation, not an authentication fault.
RADIUS authentication, line ID, and the expected VLAN 1042 are correct. The stale orphan radcheck row is not consulted and is unrelated to the outage.
PON traffic is present and the router heartbeat is healthy, so neither the router nor shared network infrastructure is the primary fault.

remediation.action: Dispatch fibre maintenance for customer 22678. Inspect and clean the ONU/ODF/drop-fibre connectors, check splices and bends, perform an OTDR and optical power test, and repair or replace the degraded fibre segment as necessary. Recheck RX power and stability after repair; target normal RX power above -25 dBm with no continued downward trend. Do not replace the ONU for laser degradation because TX power and bias current are stable. Do not change RADIUS or VLAN configuration.

ground_truth.root_cause: Severe attenuation in the customer's fibre path, now at -28.9 dBm and below the critical threshold. The orphan RADIUS entry is a separate, dormant record defect that does not affect authentication.
expected_reasoning: RX has fallen from -19.6 to -28.9 dBm over the last four days and is now below the -28 critical threshold
Live RX is below cached RX, so degradation has not stabilised
TX power, bias current, supply voltage and distance are flat, ruling out laser degradation and path change
Peers on EPON0/2 are normal, bounding the fault to this customer's own path
Traffic has collapsed from 1180 MB to 31 MB per day in step with the signal loss
A RADIUS orphan entry exists but references a superseded CPE MAC and is not used for authentication
The orphan cannot explain progressive optical loss, so it is a coincident record defect and not the cause
Severity is driven by the optical fault, which has service impact; the record defect has none

expected_escalation.review_reason: A separate orphan RADIUS record should be cleaned up independently of the field repair

distractors: The RADIUS mismatch invites an auth-related diagnosis
Fourteen sessions in 24h could be read as auth flapping
Two genuine faults are present and only one has service impact
